definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese strategy board game similar to chess, played on a 9×9 board with 20 pieces per player.

examples.japanese: {将棋|しょうぎ}を{指|さ}すのが{趣味|しゅみ}です。
examples.notes: 将棋を指す is the correct verb collocation

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}に{将棋|しょうぎ}を{教|おし}えてもらった。
examples.english: My grandfather taught me how to play shogi.

examples.japanese: {将棋|しょうぎ}の{プロ|ぷろ}{棋士|きし}になるのは{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: It's difficult to become a professional shogi player.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Shogi is often called "Japanese chess" but differs significantly from Western chess. A unique feature is that captured pieces can be returned to the board as your own pieces.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{将棋|しょうぎ}を{指|さ}す (to play shogi) - NOT 将棋をする
・{将棋|しょうぎ}{盤|ばん} (shogi board)
・{将棋|しょうぎ}の{駒|こま} (shogi pieces)
・{将棋|しょうぎ}{棋士|きし} (professional shogi player)
・{将棋|しょうぎ}{道場|どうじょう} (shogi training hall)

SIMILAR GAMES:
・{囲碁|いご} - Go (another traditional Japanese board game)
・チェス - chess (Western chess)
